topics.title: What Is a Handicap Index
topics.subtitle: Why golf has a portable number for your ability
topics.defaultPrompt: Explain what a Handicap Index actually measures, why golf invented it, and what it means to say someone is a 'scratch' golfer or a '15 handicap.' What does it predict — and what doesn't it predict?
topics.promptTemplate: Explain Handicap Index — what it measures, why golf has one, what the number actually represents, and the difference between a scratch player, a bogey golfer, and a high-handicap golfer. {{skill_level_context}} {{detail_level_context}}

options.label: Beginner
options.promptFragment: I'm new to golf — explain handicap from scratch.

options.label: Intermediate
options.promptFragment: I have a handicap already — explain what the number actually means.

options.label: Advanced
options.promptFragment: Include the statistical interpretation, why scratch is defined the way it is, and how Index relates to expected scoring distributions.

options.label: Quick Answer
options.promptFragment: Give me the concept in plain English in a few sentences.

options.label: Detailed Explanation
options.promptFragment: Walk through the concept with examples at different handicap levels.

options.label: History & Context
options.promptFragment: Tell me the story of how the handicap system evolved and why the World Handicap System was created in 2020.

topics.title: How Your Handicap Is Calculated
topics.subtitle: Score differentials, 8 of last 20, and the WHS formula
topics.defaultPrompt: Walk me through how the World Handicap System actually calculates a Handicap Index. How do score differentials work, why does WHS take the best 8 of your last 20 rounds, and what role do the soft cap and hard cap play?
topics.promptTemplate: Walk through the WHS Handicap Index calculation — score differential formula, the best 8 of last 20 averaging, the soft cap and hard cap, and how the calculation updates after each new score. {{skill_level_context}} {{detail_level_context}}

options.label: Beginner
options.promptFragment: I don't know the math yet — start from the basics.

options.label: Intermediate
options.promptFragment: Show me the formula with a worked example.

options.label: Advanced
options.promptFragment: Include the soft cap / hard cap thresholds, the playing conditions calculation (PCC), and the exceptional-score reduction.

options.label: Quick Answer
options.promptFragment: Give me the headline of the calculation in a few sentences.

options.label: Detailed Walkthrough
options.promptFragment: Walk through the formula with one worked example end-to-end.

options.label: Multiple Examples
options.promptFragment: Walk through multiple worked examples at different handicap levels so I see how the formula behaves.

topics.title: Course Handicap vs Handicap Index
topics.subtitle: Why your number changes at the tee
topics.defaultPrompt: Explain the difference between a Handicap Index and a Course Handicap. Why does my 'handicap' look different on every course and from every tee, and how do I figure out the right number to play to in a match or net competition?
topics.promptTemplate: Explain the difference between Handicap Index and Course Handicap — how the conversion is done, why it depends on the tee and the course, and how to figure out the correct number to use for a given round or competition. {{skill_level_context}} {{detail_level_context}}

options.label: Beginner
options.promptFragment: Explain why my handicap looks different in different places — I'm just learning.

options.label: Intermediate
options.promptFragment: Show me the conversion math with examples from front, middle, and back tees.

options.label: Advanced
options.promptFragment: Include the playing-handicap allowance for different formats and how net allowances vary by competition type.

options.label: Quick Answer
options.promptFragment: Give me the practical bottom line in a few sentences.

options.label: Detailed Walkthrough
options.promptFragment: Walk through Course Handicap calculation with a worked example.

options.label: Examples with Tees
options.promptFragment: Give me worked examples at the same course from different tee sets so I see how the Course Handicap moves.

topics.title: Slope and Course Rating Explained
topics.subtitle: The two numbers that grade every course
topics.defaultPrompt: Explain Course Rating and Slope Rating. What do those numbers on the scorecard actually measure, why are there two of them, and how do they get used in handicap calculations?
topics.promptTemplate: Explain Course Rating and Slope Rating — what each one measures, why both are needed, the typical ranges, and how they feed into Course Handicap and score differential calculations. {{skill_level_context}} {{detail_level_context}}

options.label: Beginner
options.promptFragment: I see these numbers on the scorecard but don't really know what they mean — start there.

options.label: Intermediate
options.promptFragment: Show me the math and how each rating is used.

options.label: Advanced
options.promptFragment: Include how courses are rated (effective playing length, obstacle factors, the rating team process) and the typical Slope range (55–155, baseline 113).

options.label: Quick Answer
options.promptFragment: Give me the headline on each rating in a couple of sentences.

options.label: Detailed Explanation
options.promptFragment: Walk through both ratings with worked examples showing the impact on Course Handicap.

options.label: Course Comparison
options.promptFragment: Compare two real-style courses — one easy, one difficult — and show how the ratings reflect the difference.

topics.title: Home Course vs Away
topics.subtitle: Why your home and travel handicap can feel different
topics.defaultPrompt: I tend to score better at my home course than at courses I travel to. Is that normal? How should I think about my handicap traveling vs at home, and what role does slope rating play in evening out home-course advantage?
topics.promptTemplate: Explain the home-vs-away handicap question — course familiarity advantage, why slope and rating are designed to normalize this, the expected score variance traveling, and how to interpret a 'travel handicap' vs your home number. {{skill_level_context}} {{detail_level_context}}

options.label: Beginner
options.promptFragment: I just play my home course — explain why travel feels harder.

options.label: Intermediate
options.promptFragment: I play a few courses regularly — explain how my Index is supposed to travel with me.

options.label: Advanced
options.promptFragment: Include research on course-familiarity effects, the typical magnitude of home-course advantage in shots, and how the WHS Slope/Rating system tries to neutralize it.

options.label: Quick Answer
options.promptFragment: Give me the practical bottom line.

options.label: Detailed Explanation
options.promptFragment: Walk through what's going on with both course familiarity and the WHS normalization.

options.label: Strategy for Travel Rounds
options.promptFragment: Give me practical advice for playing a course I've never seen — pre-round prep and on-course decisions that help close the home-course gap.

topics.title: Natural Variation in Your Scores
topics.subtitle: What your handicap predicts (and what it doesn't)
topics.defaultPrompt: If I'm a 12 handicap, what scores should I actually expect to shoot? How wide is the normal range of variation, and why do I shoot 78 one day and 95 the next on the same course?
topics.promptTemplate: Explain the natural variation in scoring around a Handicap Index — what scores a player at a given handicap actually shoots over a season, the expected distribution, why the WHS takes the best 8 of 20 (which biases toward your good days), and how to read your own variance constructively. {{skill_level_context}} {{handicap_context}} {{detail_level_context}}

options.label: Beginner
options.promptFragment: Keep the explanation simple — just help me understand why my scores swing so much.

options.label: Intermediate
options.promptFragment: I understand basic handicap math — show me what the distribution looks like.

options.label: Advanced
options.promptFragment: Include the statistical research on score variance by handicap level, standard deviation typical ranges, and what Index actually predicts statistically.

options.label: How to Think About It
options.promptFragment: Help me build a healthier mindset around the inevitable bad rounds and what they do (and don't) say about my real ability.

topics.title: Getting an Official Handicap
topics.subtitle: Signing up, posting scores, and what membership gets you
topics.defaultPrompt: Walk me through how to get an official Handicap Index. What service do I sign up with, do I need to be a club member, what does it cost, and how soon does my handicap become valid after I start posting?
topics.promptTemplate: Walk through getting an official WHS Handicap Index — which service to sign up with, club-membership requirements, typical cost, how many scores are needed before the handicap is established, and the general process for keeping it active. {{region_context}} {{detail_level_context}}

options.label: USA (GHIN)
options.promptFragment: Focus on the USA process — GHIN, USGA, allied golf associations, and typical state-level club membership routes.

options.label: UK & Ireland

options.label: Quick Answer

options.label: I'm Not a Club Member
options.promptFragment: Focus on options for getting a handicap without joining a private or full-membership club — public clubs, online clubs, regional association programs.

topics.title: Posting Scores Correctly
topics.subtitle: Net double bogey, away rounds, and exceptional scores
topics.defaultPrompt: Explain how to post scores for handicap purposes. What's net double bogey adjustment, do I post away rounds the same way, what about a round where I quit on hole 15, and what counts as an 'exceptional score'?
topics.promptTemplate: Explain posting scores correctly under WHS — net double bogey adjustment, hole-by-hole vs total-score posting, away rounds, picked-up holes, incomplete rounds, and how exceptional scores trigger the soft cap or reduction. {{skill_level_context}} {{detail_level_context}}

options.label: Beginner
options.promptFragment: I just got a handicap — walk me through how to post a score from scratch.

options.label: Intermediate
options.promptFragment: I've posted scores before but want to do it right — include the common adjustments.

options.label: Advanced

options.label: Quick Answer
options.promptFragment: Give me the must-know rules in a few sentences.

options.label: Detailed Walkthrough

options.label: Edge Cases
